title: Write-Off of Benefit Overpayment Accounts Balances
content:
Benefit Overpayment Accounts balances are written off on either of two grounds.

## Ground 1 — collection limit

Recovery stops and the remaining balance is written off when the collection limit years after the determination date have passed, counted in calendar years with a February 29 anniversary falling back to February 28.

*Hypothetical:* a determination dated 29 February 2020 with a collection limit of 6 years reaches its anniversary on 28 February 2026, there being no 29 February in 2026.

## Ground 2 — small balance

A non-fraud balance below the small-balance threshold is also written off when the days since the last recovery cover at least the small-balance inactivity months; fraud balances are never written off as small balances. The days since the last recovery are the calendar days since the latest repayment, offset or intercept on the overpayment, or since its determination date when there has been none.

| Classification | Balance below the threshold | No recovery for at least the inactivity months | Written off as a small balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-fraud | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Non-fraud | Yes | No | No |
| Non-fraud | No | Yes | No |
| Fraud | Any | Any | Never |

## Effect of a write-off

A write-off removes every remaining component and does not erase the determination; the overpayment moves from in recovery to written off. A payment later received on a written-off debt is refunded.
